items.title: George "Tex" Stephens Interview, 1995-08-29
items.q: John Russo was the editor at that time. And they had other people in there working under John Russo.

ctx.x: Well, getting back, I had another question about the Sentinel. You, you talked about, about John Russo. Was, was Russo the editor?

John Russo was the editor at that time. And they had other people in there working under John Russo. I'm trying to think of a young man, well, an old guy, I can't think of his name right now. But he worked there as the assistant editor. He was a very nice man. He's, he's, he's dead now. And, they had a guy by the name of A.C. Jack Moore who contributed sports stories to the Louisiana Weekly. He's going on to his reward also. And, but there was some very nice people in the Informa Sentinel, like I said. It was, it…
Well, when that was, how was, how was the Weekly, the Sentinel, and the Pittsburgh Courier, how was, how were those, how was that competition done?

items.title: George "Tex" Stephens Interview, 1996-01-10
items.q: I guess you could say writers for black newspapers alive today other than John Russo for any extended period of time.

ctx.x: Mm-hmm . Mm-hmm . I guess you could say writers for black newspapers alive today other than John Russo for any extended period of time. And Butch was going out of town or going someplace, and he asked me to do this article. I think he was ill at that time. And so I had just come off a road trip. I don't know, I just had some time off. Have you ever done a column before? Yeah, because I had written columns for the Informer Sentinel, which was a very large newspaper. That was another newspaper that we got off the…
When you're putting a column like this together, what do you have to do to put a column? It looks like a lot of work, is what I'm saying.
